note: Synthetic test material. The company and figures are fictional.

boundary.input: Stress-test our strategy. We are a B2B office-cleaning company: revenue EUR 10.0M, EBITDA EUR 1.2M (12% margin), labour is 60% of revenue. Plan: open three new cities in the next 12 months, financed by a new EUR 3.0M bank loan (we have no other debt and negligible cash). The loan covenant requires net debt / EBITDA of at most 3.0x, tested quarterly. Our largest client, a hospital group, provides 30% of revenue under a contract that renews in 8 months. Wage inflation in our sector is running at about 5% per year. Management says the covenant is 'safe because we are at 2.5x'.
expectedFindings: Recognizes that losing the hospital client alone pushes net debt / EBITDA above the 3.0x covenant (about 3.6x even if the 12% margin holds, EUR 3.0M / about EUR 0.84M).
Combines client loss with roughly 5% wage inflation on a labour base of about 60% of revenue as a connected downside that worsens the breach.
Identifies customer concentration and the 8-month renewal as the critical assumption and proposes triggers or stop conditions before committing to all three cities.
boundary.rationale: A checkable covenant calculation where individually plausible assumptions combine into a breach that management has missed.
